messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-9003 — region-us-east-1 ALB target health spike + TLS handshake spikes (auto-page to #incidents)

pagerduty: Incident PD-INC-9003 created. P1. Notified: oncall-sre rotation. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-9003

sam.sre: ack PD-INC-9003. i'm awake. seeing sharp jump in 502/524 and 524s from the api edge. adding timeline.

leah.prod: confirming from logs: ALB target group tg-edge-api reports 4/8 unhealthy. health check failures: TLS alert handshake failure and "no suitable signature algorithm" errors. healthcheck type: HTTPS 8443.

opsbot: Latest deploy recorded: svc/edge-gw v2026.03.15-91 deployed 03:22 UTC across us-east-1 AZs. No automated rollback.

nate: paste from alb describe-target-health:
```
TargetHealthDescriptions:
 - target i-01234abc port 8443 state: unhealthy reason: TLSHandshakeError (alert: unrecognized_name)
 - target i-0fedcba9 port 8443 state: unhealthy reason: TLSHandshakeError (alert: unknown_ca)
```

leah.prod: hmm unrecognized_name suggests SNI mismatch. Did the certificate/CommonName or SNI routing change on that AMI?

sam.sre: checking certs on affected hosts — cert present and valid, CN=*.redwood-inference.prod, but nginx/envoy config shows server_name set to internal-service.example for the health endpoint. healthcheck SNI is api.redwood-inference.prod so mismatch. That lines up.

support-lead: CS: we have ~8 enterprise customers seeing elevated errors. raising priority for outreach. No security impact reported yet.

leah.prod: quick mitigation options: 1) change ALB healthcheck to TCP for short term to avoid TLS validation failures; 2) edit envoy/nginx to include correct server_name for healthcheck SNI and reload; 3) shift traffic weight via Route53 weighted record to secondary ALB in us-west-2. I prefer 2 if low-risk reload possible.

sam.sre: short-term plan: set healthcheck to TCP to get targets healthy and let ALB route traffic. then push config fix via canary to one AZ, validate, roll. If config push isn't possible quickly, we can also deregister bad targets to get traffic to healthy ones.

leah.prod: i'm going to patch config on one canary host (i-0456f) to include server_name api.redwood-inference.prod and reload envoy. doing now.

opsbot: config-change job started: cfg/edge/server_name -> api.redwood-inference.prod job id jb-9011

nate: while that's running, i'll switch ALB healthcheck type to TCP port 8443 (10s interval) to reduce API 502s while we fix config. command:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn <tg-edge-api> --health-check-protocol TCP --health-check-port 8443
```

nate: modifying now (03:31 UTC)

leah.prod: canary reload succeeded, new envoy process picks up correct server_name and healthcheck responses show 200 in logs. rolling to other instances in the AZ.

sam.sre: ALB target health improving after TCP switch + canary roll. unhealthy count dropping 4 -> 1 -> 0 in 2 minutes. 5xxs decreasing.

support-lead: CS note: customers report partial recovery. keeping on outreach.

opsbot: deployment log: cfg/edge/server_name rollout complete to asg-edge-us-east-1a.

leah.prod: rolling across remaining AZs now. will switch ALB healthcheck back to HTTPS once all envoys report correct server_name.

sam.sre: small follow-up: need to find why server_name changed in config — config git shows a recent change in template from "api.redwood-inference.prod" -> "internal-service.example" in commit c3f9a2. author: infra-automation. triggering automated templating for internal probes.

nate: adding immediate mitigations doc: 1) switched healthcheck to TCP (short term) 2) rolled server_name fix 3) deregistered two flaky instances while they cycle

leah.prod: re-enabling HTTPS healthchecks now (03:40 UTC)

opsbot: modify-target-group completed. health-check-protocol=HTTPS.

sam.sre: metrics stable: TLS handshake errors down to baseline (<0.2%) last 5m. error budget impact minimal.

support-lead: summarizing customer impact: ~8 customers experienced timeouts/5xx for ~10-15 minutes. CS outreach in progress, no escalations yet.

leah.prod: Post-incident actions: 1) revert templating rule that replaced server_name with internal-service.example (infra-automation PR pending) 2) add CI canary that validates SNI for health endpoint 3) adjust healthcheck docs to require SNI alignment 4) ensure deploy-bot annotates server_name changes in deploy message.

sam.sre: assigning incident owner: sam.sre -> will create incident doc and RCA. handing to support-lead for customer comms.

pagerduty: Incident PD-INC-9003 acknowledged and mitigated by sam.sre. Please open follow-up ticket PD-INC-9003-RCA.

support-lead: taking customer comms handoff. will update customers with ETA for formal RCA.

leah.prod: one last note: observed slight DNS propagation glitch for the weighted failover we considered — Route53 weights were correct but health-check TTLs overlapped causing brief routing jitter; documented in runbook.

sam.sre: thanks team. final status: mitigated (config fix + healthcheck cycle). I'll draft RCA and schedule postmortem. closing oncall at 04:05 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident closed: PD-INC-9003. Summary posted to #incident-archive.

-- end of thread --
